org.name: CyberWareX
org.summary: A suite of x402-native services built for autonomous AI agents. Every endpoint speaks x402: your agent hits it, gets a 402 price quote, settles in USDC on Base, and receives the result. No accounts, no API keys, no humans in the loop.

payment.note: Unpaid call returns HTTP 402 with an x402 price quote; sign the USDC EIP-3009 authorization and retry with the X-PAYMENT header. Gasless for the payer.

use_when: Reach for it when your agent must read a page it was handed, scrape live data, screenshot a site for a report, or turn a URL into a PDF - any time the answer lives on a website the model can't see.

Extract elements by CSS selector

Render a page to PDF

tools.name: defi-oracle
tools.title: DeFi Safety Oracle
tools.description: Answer 'is this token safe to trade?' before committing funds. Deterministic, evidence-carrying rug/honeypot risk assessment across 6 EVM chains (Base, BSC, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Robinhood Chain): live buy/sell simulation, contract powers (upgradeable proxy, owner mint/pause/blacklist), plus a GoPlus/honeypot.is cross-check. Grade A-F + tradeable flag. Free trial: first 3 calls/day per IP with the 'X-Free-Trial: 1' header - no wallet needed to evaluate. Now with a privilege graph (who can upgrade/mint/pause) and dynamic-tax mutability detection. Deep /v1/risk/check runs an adversarial simulation matrix (buy->sell across trade sizes x caller wallets) to catch size- and address-gated honeypots a single probe misses.
use_when: Call it before any swap, token approval, or 'should I buy this' decision - it catches honeypots and hidden sell-taxes so your agent never buys a coin it can't sell.

endpoints.desc: Contract powers + ownership analysis
Live buy/sell honeypot simulation
Full safety report (all of the above)
Batch screen up to 25 tokens in one POST
Agent verdict: ALLOW/LIMIT/RECHECK/BLOCK + reason codes
Full multi-dimensional risk decomposition for agents

One-call launch screening: GREEN/CAUTION/BLOCK (allow/review/reject) + reasons, incl. deployer prior-scams & code-rugged-before. For launchpads: auto-reject rugs before listing. Cache-first (~$0 on repeats)
Deployer-wallet reputation from our verdict ledger: prior proven honeypot/scam tokens (dead launches excluded)
Contract-template reputation: honeypot/scam siblings sharing this bytecode fingerprint (fuzzy-matched)

tools.mcp: Official MCP registry: io.github.CyberPunk11147/cyberwarex-defi-oracle - tools: token_safety, honeypot_check, contract_risk (install via registry.modelcontextprotocol.io)

tools.name: tx-sim
tools.title: Transaction Simulator
tools.description: Decode an unsigned transaction and know what it does BEFORE signing. Given a chain, to, value and calldata, it decodes the function and arguments, flags dangerous actions (unlimited token approvals, setApprovalForAll, ownership transfers, native-value drains), and runs a keyless eth_call preview reporting whether the transaction would succeed or revert. Works across Base, BSC, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum and Optimism. Deterministic, read-only, no keys. Free trial: 3 calls/day per IP with the 'X-Free-Trial: 1' header. The essential pre-sign safety check for any trading or wallet agent.
use_when: Call it right before signing any transaction - preview exactly what it will do and flag risky actions so your agent doesn't sign a drainer.

endpoints.desc: Pre-sign Safety Firewall: one GREEN/REVIEW/BLOCK verdict fusing tx decode+sim, signature-drainer, address-risk, URL-phishing and token-safety. Call before signing anything.
Decode + risk flags + eth_call would-succeed/revert preview
Calldata decode + risk flags (no simulation, cheaper)

tools.name: sig-decoder
tools.title: Signature Decoder
tools.description: Pay-per-call decoder for off-chain signature requests: turn an opaque EIP-712 typed-data request (eth_signTypedData_v4) or a personal_sign string into a human-readable summary plus security risk flags for the drainer patterns wallets miss - gasless unlimited token approvals (EIP-2612 Permit, DAI permit, Uniswap Permit2) and asset-transferring marketplace orders (Seaport). Keyless, deterministic, no network.
use_when: Use it before approving an off-chain signature (Permit, Permit2, Seaport) - it decodes what you're really authorizing and flags drainer patterns.

endpoints.desc: Decode an EIP-712 typed-data or personal_sign request into a summary + security risk flags.
